title: Brunch
novel:
Ted's parents [[visited|visit]] New York for [[brunch|brunch]], and he was [[thrilled|thrill]] — until his mom and dad started [[bickering|bicker]] over the [[menu|menu]]. His mother, Virginia, [[kept correcting|keep correct]] his father's [[grammar|grammar]]. His father, Alfred, rolled his eyes and [[muttered|mutter]] about his wife's "helpful [[suggestions|suggestion]]."

Robin found the whole scene [[hilarious|hilarious]]. She had never seen Ted so [[embarrassed|embarrass]]. "They're worse than my parents during [[divorce|divorce]]," she joked. But Ted was not laughing. He had always [[portrayed|portray]] his parents as the perfect [[couple|couple]], and now they were [[crumbling|crumble]] in front of him.

Marshall, meanwhile, was still [[navigating|navigate]] his [[complicated|complicated]] situation with Lily. She was sleeping on the couch, and every morning was an [[exercise|exercise]] in [[awkward|awkward]] [[silence|silence]].

During brunch, Virginia [[confessed|confess]] that she and Alfred had been seeing a [[therapist|therapist]]. Ted nearly [[choked|choke]] on his [[pancake|pancake]]. "Since when?" he asked. "Since you went to college," his mother replied. "We stayed together for you."

Ted felt the ground [[shift|shift]] beneath him. Everything he believed about love had been [[built|build]] on a [[myth|myth]]. But then his father reached across the table and held Virginia's hand. "We're still here, [[aren't we|be not we]]?" he said. And in that simple [[gesture|gesture]], Ted saw something more honest than perfection — he saw [[commitment|commitment]].

visit.en: to go to see a person or place for a short time

brunch.en: a late-morning meal that replaces breakfast and lunch

thrill.en: to make someone feel very excited and happy

bicker.en: to argue about things that are not important

menu.en: a list of food you can order at a restaurant

keep correct.en: to repeatedly tell someone they made a mistake

grammar.en: the rules about how words change and combine in a language

mutter.en: to speak quietly, especially when you are annoyed

suggestion.en: an idea or plan that you offer for someone to consider

embarrass.en: to make someone feel ashamed or shy

divorce.en: the legal ending of a marriage

portray.en: to describe or show someone in a particular way

couple.en: two people who are married or in a romantic relationship

crumble.en: to break into small pieces; to stop existing

navigate.en: to find your way through a difficult situation

complicated.en: difficult to understand or deal with

exercise.en: an activity that tests or improves a skill

silence.en: a period of time when no one speaks

therapist.en: a professional who helps people deal with emotional problems

choke.en: to be unable to breathe because something blocks your throat

pancake.en: a thin flat round food made from batter and fried

shift.en: to move or change position; to change opinion

build.en: to make something by putting parts together

myth.en: a popular belief that is not true

aren't we.en: used to ask for agreement or confirmation

gesture.en: a movement of your hands or body that shows a feeling

commitment.en: a promise to do something or to stay with someone
